---
title: "Association testing: relatedness modelled, not removed"
description: "Compare pruning related individuals with keeping them in a whole-genome regression, on the same variants"
---

```{r}
#| include: false
source(file.path(Sys.getenv("QUARTO_PROJECT_DIR", "../.."), "R/facts.R"))
S  <- "04C_association_other"
cmp <- tab(S, "pdac_demo_regenie_comparison.tsv")
cmp$key <- substr(cmp$analysis, 1, 1); rownames(cmp) <- cmp$key
if (!identical(sort(cmp$key), c("A", "B", "C", "D"))) stop("expected analyses A to D")
g <- function(k, col) cmp[k, col]
n_of <- function(k) g(k, "cases") + g(k, "controls")
rm_cases <- g("B", "cases") - g("A", "cases"); rm_ctrl <- g("B", "controls") - g("A", "controls")
n_var <- unique(cmp$variants); if (length(n_var) != 1) stop("analyses A to D differ in variant count")
ABO <- "9:133273682:A:T"
# Section 4A primary scan, for the contrast with analysis A
S4 <- "04A_association_binary"
lam4a <- val(S4, "pdac_demo_04A_lambda.tsv", "lambda_gc")
var4a <- val(S4, "pdac_demo_04A_lambda.tsv", "variants_tested")
k4a   <- as.integer(read.table(res(S4, "pdac_demo_04A_npc_chosen.txt"))[1, 2])
sc4a  <- tab(S4, "pdac_demo_04A_npc_scans.tsv")
th4a  <- tab(S4, "pdac_demo_04A_top_hits.tsv"); p4a <- th4a$P[th4a$ID == ABO]
sr <- tab(S4, "pdac_demo_04A_sens_relatedness.tsv")
srp <- sr[grepl("^phenotype-aware", sr$rule), ]; srk <- sr[grepl("king-cutoff", sr$rule), ]
# Section 8: spread of lambda of the European scan over replicate phenotypes
ls8 <- tab("08_replicates", "pdac_demo_08_lambda_summary.tsv"); rownames(ls8) <- ls8$lambda
sd8 <- ls8["lambda_eur_4a", "sd"]
ls8_n <- nrow(tab("08_replicates", "pdac_demo_08_lambda.tsv"))
```

Section 1B removed related individuals so that the case-control scan could assume independence.
In a rare cancer every individual removed is information lost, and the rule used here removes
controls preferentially to keep cases, which shifts the case-control balance as well. The
alternative is to keep the related individuals and model the relatedness, which is what
whole-genome regression in REGENIE does. This page asks what the pruning bought.

Running REGENIE on the post-QC data would answer nothing, because the relatives are already gone.
The comparison therefore goes back to the European set before relatedness pruning.

```bash
how-to-gwas-pdac/
├── sections/04C_association_other/   # script and committed results
└── results/regenie/                  # where the script writes
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Before you start"}
Finish [Association testing: case-control](../04A_association_binary/04A_association_binary.qmd).
REGENIE 4.1.2 is installed by the project's tool set-up. The script sits directly in
`sections/04C_association_other/` and is run from the repository root, as
`scripts/dev/run_all.sh` runs it.
:::

---

## 01 - Four analyses on the same variants

```bash
bash sections/04C_association_other/01_regenie_wgr.sh
```

| | Individuals | Relatedness | Method |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | after pruning | none left | logistic regression, PLINK 2, Firth fallback |
| **B** | before pruning | ignored | logistic regression, PLINK 2, Firth fallback |
| **C** | before pruning | modelled | REGENIE, step 1 ridge predictor as a leave-one-chromosome-out offset, Firth correction |
| **D** | before pruning | ignored | REGENIE without the offset (`--ignore-pred`), Firth correction |

All four use the same `r num(n_var)` variants and the same covariates: SEX, AGE and ten
components, the script's default (`N_PC`). Each comparison isolates one thing:

- **A against B** is the whole pruning decision. It is a compound contrast: the sets differ in
  size and in balance.
- **B against C** tests the mixed model: the same individuals, relatedness ignored against
  modelled.
- **D** separates the software from the method. B against D is PLINK 2 against REGENIE with no
  offset; D against C is the offset alone.

---

## 02 - The result

| Analysis | Cases | Controls | Effective N | λ | *P* < 5 × 10⁻⁸ | *P* < 1 × 10⁻⁵ | *P*, causal *ABO* variant |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
`r paste(sprintf("| %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %d | %d | %s |", cmp$analysis, num(cmp$cases), num(cmp$controls), dec(cmp$neff, 1), dec(cmp$lambda, 4), cmp$sig_5e8, cmp$sugg_1e5, sapply(cmp$P_causal, sci)), collapse = "\n")`

**What the pruning cost.** Keeping the relatives adds `r num(n_of("B") - n_of("A"))` individuals, `r num(rm_cases)` cases and
`r num(rm_ctrl)` controls, and raises the effective sample size from `r dec(g("A", "neff"), 1)` to `r dec(g("B", "neff"), 1)`. The causal
variant's *P* goes from `r sci(g("A", "P_causal"))` to `r sci(g("B", "P_causal"))`, and λ does not rise (`r dec(g("A", "lambda"), 4)` against
`r dec(g("B", "lambda"), 4)`). On these data the retained relatedness cost nothing in calibration, and the pruning
discarded information for no statistical gain.

**What the mixed model did.** On the same individuals, modelling relatedness (C) moves λ from
`r dec(g("B", "lambda"), 4)` to `r dec(g("C", "lambda"), 4)`. REGENIE without the offset (D) gives `r dec(g("D", "lambda"), 4)`, close to PLINK 2 on
the same people, so the difference between B and C is the offset, not the software. A mixed model
that raises λ has not removed structure. The causal *ABO* variant is tested against an offset built
without chromosome 9; its *P* is `r sci(g("C", "P_causal"))` in C, against `r sci(g("D", "P_causal"))` in D, the same software without the
offset. Whether the
rise in λ elsewhere comes from offsets that contain the causal loci, or from the behaviour of the
offset in a trait with no polygenic background, this comparison alone cannot say.

::: {.callout-important title="Why the offset behaves this way here"}
The demonstration phenotype was simulated from a few causal variants and no polygenic background.
Step 1 of REGENIE fits a whole-genome ridge regression to capture polygenic signal; with none to
capture, the predictor it builds can reflect only the causal loci and chance. The
leave-one-chromosome-out scheme keeps a locus out of the offset used for its own chromosome, but
every other chromosome is tested against an offset that contains it. Step 1 prints its
cross-validated R² in `results/regenie/pdac_demo_regenie_C_step1.log`; read it before taking C as a
test of the method. In a real polygenic trait the same comparison is the informative one, and the
result can go the other way.
:::

---

## 03 - How this sits next to Section 4A

Analysis A is not the primary scan of Section 4A. It uses ten components and this script's variant
filter, where Section 4A uses PC1-PC`r k4a`, chosen by its step 01b, on `r num(var4a)` variants:

| | Components | Variants | λ | *P*, causal *ABO* variant |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Section 4A, primary | PC1-PC`r k4a` | `r num(var4a)` | `r dec(lam4a, 4)` | `r sci(p4a)` |
| Section 4A, step 01b scan with ten components | PC1-PC10 | `r num(sc4a$variants[sc4a$n_pcs == 10])` | `r dec(sc4a$lambda[sc4a$n_pcs == 10], 4)` | |
| This page, analysis A | PC1-PC10 | `r num(n_var)` | `r dec(g("A", "lambda"), 4)` | `r sci(g("A", "P_causal"))` |

Section 4A also compares two pruning rules for relatedness: the phenotype-aware rule of the
pipeline, which removes, across all ancestries, `r num(srp$removed)` individuals (`r num(srp$removed_cases)` cases, `r num(srp$removed_controls)` controls), and the default
`--king-cutoff` of PLINK 2, which removes `r num(srk$removed)` (`r num(srk$removed_cases)` cases, `r num(srk$removed_controls)` controls), with λ of
`r dec(srp$lambda, 4)` and `r dec(srk$lambda, 4)` (`pdac_demo_04A_sens_relatedness.tsv`). The two pages agree: in these data relatedness is a
question of information, not of calibration.

---

## Limits of this demonstration

- One draw of the phenotype. For scale, over `r ls8_n` replicate phenotypes on the same genotypes the
  standard deviation of λ of the European scan, on LD-pruned variants, is `r dec(sd8, 4)`
  ([Replicates](../08_replicates/08_replicates.qmd)). The differences A against B and B against C
  are `r dec(abs(g("A", "lambda") - g("B", "lambda")) / sd8, 1)` and `r dec(abs(g("C", "lambda") - g("B", "lambda")) / sd8, 1)` times that. The four analyses share
  the draw, so their differences are paired and less noisy than that standard deviation suggests,
  but one draw cannot show how stable the ordering is.
- The demonstration data are not a real case series. In a real one relatives may be concentrated
  among cases, and the amount of relatedness can be far larger.
- No polygenic background (callout above), so C is a fair test of the software and of the
  offset, but not of the method's benefit in a polygenic trait.
- The step 1 log is not committed, because it records local paths; the R² it prints is
  therefore not quoted on this page.
- The script is not copied by the project set-up of [Getting started](../../getting_started.qmd),
  which copies only `scripts/` folders; run it from a clone of the repository.

## Key decisions on this page

- Prune relatives, or keep them and model relatedness.
- If pruning, which rule: one that protects cases changes the balance as well as the size.
- If modelling, whether the step 1 predictor captures polygenic signal or absorbs the loci of
  interest, judged from its cross-validated R² and from λ with and without the offset.
